LESSON: ATHLETICS AND MOSAIC

Grade: Grade 9
Subject: CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS
Strand: Creating and Performing
Topic 2.3: Athletics and Mosaic
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Athletics and Mosaic, part of Creating and Performing in Grade 9 CREATIVE ARTS AND SPORTS.

Key inquiry question: How has long distance running benefitted Kenya? 2. Why is it important to follow the phases of jumping in triple jump?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. observe a live or virtual performance of Triple jump to identify the phases,

2. demonstrate the approach, take off, flight and landing phases in Triple jump,

3. practise triple jump skills in athletics,

4. practise technique used in long distance running while observing safety,

5. observe others’ performance in Triple jump and long distance running skills and give feedback.

6. collaboratively, play games or engage in athletic events

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. observe a live or virtual performance of Triple jump to identify the phases,
2. demonstrate the approach, take off, flight and landing phases in Triple jump,
3. practise triple jump skills in athletics,
4. practise technique used in long distance running while observing safety,
5. observe others’ performance in Triple jump and long distance running skills and give feedback.
6. collaboratively, play games or engage in athletic events

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Athletics and Mosaic together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: the learner gains knowledge performing Triple jump and long distance running skills and gives feedback

to enhance confidence.

• Self-efficacy: the learner shows confidence in taking up new challenges and believes in performing new skills in athletics.

• Critical Thinking and Problem Solving: learners make decisions and decide on the skill to apply at a particular phase while

running long distance.

• Creativity and Imagination: the learner creates an artistic themed mosaic composition for describing the long distance races.

• Citizenship: the learner searches and makes a mosaic of Kenyan long distance athletes.

13

Values:
• Love: the learner shows love for the country as they identify and appreciate a Kenyan athlete and make a mosaic composition.

• Responsibility: the learner cares for self and others, as they participate in skills for long distance running and triple jump

while observing safety.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Social Cohesion- the learner engages in various creative arts and sports activities, appreciating the diverse cultures and values

from different communities to enhance social cohesion.

• Citizenship: learner appreciates Kenyan athletes as they create mosaic compositions of their favourite Kenyan athletes.

Link to other learning areas:

• English: language skills are applied when the learner discusses different techniques in long-distance races, enhancing their

ability to express ideas clearly.

• Mathematics: Analysing the pacing, speed, and strategies involved in long-distance races incorporates mathematical

concepts into the learning process.

• Pre-Technical Studies: the learner interacts with digital devices when searching Kenyan athletes.
